subject: Cloudline renewal — competitive replacement concern and proposed mitigation
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudline.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal + vendor bake-off

Hi Priyom,

Quick note ahead of our renewal in August. Execs just flagged an aggressive proposal from RivalAI — they're promising a 40% cost reduction and a sub-60ms 95th latency in our pilot tests. I don't have the full bench yet, but they're pressuring for a bake-off window in July.

We love Redwood's reliability and the work you've done on our caching profiles, but procurement is asking for a plan that addresses both price and demonstrable perf improvements.

Can you: 1) confirm what perf numbers we can guarantee for our current workload (p95 latency and token cost) for the Pilot cluster, and 2) share a short retention/save proposal we can present to the procurement committee?

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks,
Samira
VP Product Operations, Cloudline Retail
---
Samira Khan
samira.k@cloudline.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal + vendor bake-off

Samira — thanks for the heads up and for flagging the competitive pressure. We're on this. High level: we can commit to an A/B pilot that reproduces your production request mix and run it back-to-back with RivalAI. That will give you apples-to-apples p95 and cost numbers.

Immediate next steps I propose (short list for procurement):
- Redwood-run benchmark (72h steady-state) using your prod sampling (we use your sandbox tokens)
- Live latency dashboard access for Cloudline during the bake-off
- A short-term retention offer: 12-month renewal with a blended unit price guarantee + a one-time onboarding credit tied to performance SLAs.

I'm looping Marissa and Ben to scope the benchmark and craft the commercial language. We have a recent internal benchmark pack that addresses quantization and batching tradeoffs — I'll attach the summary.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-benchmark-report-Q2-2028.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Upcoming renewal + vendor bake-off

Folks — forwarding Samira's note and Priyom's reply. I pulled the most relevant perf slices from the Q2 pack and sketched a save plan draft. Key points:

- Baseline: production-sampled p95 = 78ms, median = 18ms, predictable token cost ~$0.0018/token after caching. (See attached excerpt for distribution).
- RivalAI claim looks like it assumes much shorter sequences and heavy quantization on the model family that breaks on your longer dialogues. Our pilot should use your 99th-percentile conversation length to be fair.
- Proposed save play: 10% platform credit for the first 3 months + 6% list-price reduction for renewals >= 12 months, plus a one-time SLO credit for missed monthly p95 targets during the first quarter.

I've also draft-scribed the SOW changes to clarify rollout windows and rollback triggers — attaching CL-SOW-draft-v2.docx and SOC2 evidence excerpt.

If Ben can confirm capacity for a July 9–12 bake-off window (we need a dedicated pilot pool), I'll finalize the commercial language for Priyom to send to Samira.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Attachments: CL-SOW-draft-v2.docx; SOC2-evidence-excerpt-2028.txt

> On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 11:02 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samira — thanks for the heads up and for flagging the competitive pressure. We're on this....

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Upcoming renewal + vendor bake-off

Can confirm capacity — we can allocate a 4-GPU pilot pool for July 9–12 and mirror Cloudline's production ingress. Notes:
- We should pin model weights to the same checkpoint RivalAI claims to use; otherwise results will be noisy. Ops will capture identical sequence seeds and KV cache priming to ensure parity.
- I recommend we offer an extended latency SLA of p95 < 85ms for the pilot, tied to a one-time credit if missed. That gives procurement something measurable without overpromising.

I'll put the pilot runbook and dashboard share together — target to have it in Samira's hands by EOD June 22.

Ben
Principal Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudline.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal + vendor bake-off

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifying points from procurement and engineering after reviewing your attachments:

1) Procurement: the blended unit price for 12 months + onboarding credit looks promising. Can you spell out the exact credit mechanism (credit dollars vs token rebate) and the renewal breakpoint that triggers the 6% list reduction? We'd like that as a bullet in the commercial term sheet.

2) Engineering: the RivalAI bench they showed us used much smaller batch sizes and a non-streaming path. We're happy to run the full-length test you propose, but we need the dashboard and raw run logs for independent review. Can you provide the run logs (redacted) and a SOC2 evidence excerpt ahead of the bake-off?

If those two items are in place I'll recommend procurement greenlight the bake-off window. Also looping in James Peters from RivalAI — I'd like both vendors present for the July run so procurement can watch the same dashboards live.

Samira
---
Attachments requested: Redwood-benchmark-report-Q2-2028.pdf (already provided), SOC2-evidence-excerpt-2028.txt (please provide), CL-SOW-draft-v2.docx (we received)
